answer: An IPFS CID addresses content by its hash, so retrieval proves the content matches the address. The hash is verified on retrieval, and the content must match the CID. The knoll signal separates the two cases at a glance: A farm needs 345 separate CIDs, since one hash cannot address 345 different contents. The dawn ledger records each payment, the kernel window resets the board, and 345 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
